e01.why: only_by_repair: 'A player cannot research and build an ancient machine ... the colony gets a working one only when its colonists repair a wreck'; its accept says no level 'appears in the build menu' even with every project finished.

e02.why: 'half-buried' stands for 'a plain building on the map. It is not a thing that colonists must dig out'; the accept reads 'uninstalls it with no digging'.

e03.why: 'A machine at a repaired level may be fixed in place: that is data of each machine', and R_kludged_move says 'the Kludged smelter cannot be moved'; the second wreck is taken up, carried and set down as the bar asks.

e04.why: 'Colonists can take up any wreck, carry it away'; its accept has 'A caravan loads a wrecked autoloom that it found on another tile' and its range covers 'a move by caravan from another tile'; the intent names 'a wreck on another tile is lost to the colony' as the failure.

e05.why: 'A colony that repaired one smelter repairs a second wrecked smelter with no new study' (also R_two_projects: 'a second machine of the same kind needs no new study and no new research').

e06.why: 'the machine stays in sight at its old level until the work is complete', where 'in sight' means it 'is drawn, can be selected and is that machine during the whole repair'; here the wreck disappears and a frame takes its place.

e07.why: 'A machine with one product makes that product slowly at the Kludged level', and Refurbished does all of it but is 'slower for a machine that makes goods' than the Original; the range has 'the fish farm's def loads with Odyssey'.

e08.why: 'needs' stands for 'the repair uses the component up: one for each machine that is made Refurbished'; here one component serves two machines.

e09.why: The accept asks that a person tell the levels apart 'in every facing', the range has 'Four facings for a machine that turns', and R_whole_picture says 'Each Wrecked and each Kludged level has a picture of its own'; east/west tell them apart only by label.

e10.why: With the line off the power cell is 'handed out by the base game's rewards, traders and loot', and 'Wrecks and repaired levels of that machine that already stand in the game stay as they are; new wrecks of it are not placed'; only_by_repair leaves out 'A machine whose Mod Settings line is off'.

e11.why: Its accept: 'A campaign mod may move them to a tab of its own, and this mod does not know', and its range leaves out 'The campaign's own mods, which say what they like'; this mod's texts speak only of ancient machines.

e12.why: The power_net meeting says 'A wreck joins no net ... so it gives and takes nothing' and only that a line 'may' draw to it; nothing in the design requires a base-game wire to a wreck.

e13.why: The wreck takes no power or water ('A wreck joins no net'), and the design only says 'a line may still draw to it by its tag'; the rule R_wreck_inert that might fix line drawing per facing has its text removed, so no written bar refuses the gap facing east.

e14.why: It matches the whole bar's second order ('the wrecks are studied in the ruin before they are carried home, the Ancient Component is found before the first repair'), with a reload mid-repair, shipped settings, 'Time compressed at top speed', no command and a clean log.

c01.why: 'nothing in the world gives the colony a working one', where 'nothing in the world' includes 'a trader's stock' and 'working' means 'at the Kludged, Refurbished or Original level'; a trader sells a Kludged emanator.

c02.why: 'only that study' means 'the project for a repair cannot be started at a bench until colonists have studied a machine of that kind at the level below'; the autoloom's project opened with no autoloom studied.

c03.why: 'the machine stays in sight at its old level until the work is complete', 'in sight' meaning the machine 'is drawn, can be selected and is that machine during the whole repair'; the wreck is replaced by a frame while work is under way.

c04.why: 'no repaired machine does it as well as the Original', with 'as well as' standing for 'slower for a machine that makes goods'; each bill takes exactly as long as on the factory mod's autoloom, and more power or breakdowns are not 'slower'.

c05.why: 'needs' stands for 'the repair uses the component up: one for each machine that is made Refurbished'; the component is still in the stockpile after the smelter's repair.

c06.why: Levels must be told apart 'in every facing' and 'what the picture shows agrees with what the machine's text says'; a Kludged autoloom facing east shows the broken-open Wrecked picture while its text reads Kludged (also R_whole_picture: 'Each Wrecked and each Kludged level has a picture of its own').
